name: ldm_validate_privheads
prose: Real signature is ldm_validate_privheads(state, ph1), where ph1 is a single struct privhead pointer, not an array. Precondition: state is a valid parsed_partitions with a valid state->disk, ph1 points to caller-owned writable storage for one struct privhead; both are non-NULL (the function BUGs otherwise); the function may sleep (kmalloc GFP_KERNEL, sector reads). Postcondition: returns true only if all of the following hold, otherwise false (with a message logged). It allocates two scratch privheads, failing (false) if either allocation fails. It sets ph1->config_start = 0, then for i = 0, 1, 2 reads the sector at ph1->config_start + off[i] (OFF_PRIV1, OFF_PRIV2, OFF_PRIV3; for i >= 1 config_start is the value parsed from the first PRIVHEAD) and parses it with ldm_parse_privhead into ph1 (i = 0) or the i-th scratch privhead; a failed sector read, or a failed parse of the first or second PRIVHEAD, returns false; a failed parse of the third PRIVHEAD is only logged and ignored. It then requires that the database fits the disk (ph1->config_start <= get_capacity(state->disk) and config_start + config_size <= capacity), that the logical disk area ends before the database (logical_disk_start <= config_start and logical_disk_start + logical_disk_size <= config_start), and that ldm_compare_privheads(ph1, first scratch privhead) succeeds. The scratch privheads are always freed before return; each sector obtained is released with put_dev_sector. On true, ph1 holds the validated primary PRIVHEAD; on false the contents of ph1 are not meaningful.
note: Slice head cut; prior prose misdescribed the second parameter as an array of three privhead pointers.

name: add_of_partition
prose: Precondition: state is a valid parsed_partitions, slot is a valid index with slot < state->limit, np is a device_node for which validate_of_partition succeeded (it has a "reg" property of the expected length whose address and size are 512-byte aligned and whose size is non-zero), and np has a "label" property or, failing that, a "name" property so the string passed to strscpy is non-NULL. Postcondition: returns nothing. It reads the offset and size from reg (a_cells/s_cells cells) and calls put_partition(state, slot, offset / 512, size / 512). If np has the boolean property "read-only" it sets ADDPART_FLAG_READONLY in state->parts[slot].flags (never clears flags). It copies the string of property "label" (or, when absent, the "name" property) into state->parts[slot].info.volname with strscpy, truncating to sizeof(volname) - 1 characters and NUL-terminating, and appends "(volname)" (truncated to the temporary buffer) to state->pp_buf with strlcat bounded by PAGE_SIZE. No reference, memory or lock is acquired or released.

name: opal_send_recv
prose: Precondition: dev is a valid initialised opal_dev (its send_recv callback is set, used by opal_send_cmd/opal_recv_cmd) and cont is a non-NULL continuation callable as cont(dev); the caller may sleep. Postcondition: it calls opal_send_cmd(dev); if that returns non-zero it returns that value; otherwise it calls opal_recv_cmd(dev) and returns a non-zero result; otherwise it calls opal_recv_check(dev) and returns a non-zero result; otherwise it returns cont(dev), whatever int that call returns (cont is called exactly once, only when all three previous calls returned 0). It holds no lock or reference of its own.

name: crypto_aead_setauthsize
prose: Precondition: tfm is a valid crypto_aead transform; authsize is any unsigned int. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL, leaving tfm->authsize unchanged, if authsize exceeds crypto_aead_maxauthsize(tfm) or if authsize is 0 while the maximum is non-zero. Otherwise, if the algorithm provides a setauthsize hook it is called with (tfm, authsize) and a non-zero result is returned with tfm->authsize left unchanged; if the hook is absent or returns 0, tfm->authsize is set to authsize and 0 is returned. No lock or reference is acquired or released.

name: aegis128_do_simd
prose: Precondition: none (the result depends on the calling context). Postcondition: if the kernel is built with CONFIG_CRYPTO_AEGIS128_SIMD and the have_simd static branch is enabled, returns the value of crypto_simd_usable() (true iff SIMD registers may currently be used in this context); otherwise (no SIMD config or have_simd disabled) returns false. No side effects; no lock, reference or memory is acquired or released.

name: crypto_ahash_update
prose: Precondition: req is an ahash_request that was initialised (crypto_ahash_init) with a valid tfm and whose input (req->src scatterlist or req->svirt virtual buffer) covers req->nbytes bytes; the caller handles the asynchronous completion callback. Postcondition, by case: (1) if tfm->using_shash, returns shash_ahash_update(req, ahash_request_ctx(req)). (2) Else if req is on the stack and the tfm is asynchronous, returns -EAGAIN and does nothing. (3) Else if the tfm is not block-only, returns ahash_do_req_chain(req, &alg->update): the update op result directly when the tfm supports virtual addresses or the request is not virtual, else a fallback result or -ENOSYS if the fallback cannot be used. (4) Otherwise (block-only tfm) let blen be the byte count cached at the end of the request context, bs the block size and nonzero the CRYPTO_AHASH_ALG_FINAL_NONZERO flag (0 or 1): if blen + req->nbytes < bs + nonzero the input is appended to the cache, the cached count is increased by req->nbytes, nothing is hashed, req->nbytes is unchanged and 0 is returned. (5) Else any cached bytes are prepended to the data through req->sg_head (req->src = req->sg_head, req->nbytes += blen), req->nbytes is reduced by nonzero, the caller completion and data are saved and replaced by ahash_update_done, and the update is submitted via ahash_do_req_chain: if it returns -EINPROGRESS or -EBUSY that value is returned and completion happens later in ahash_update_done (which performs the same finish step); otherwise ahash_update_finish(req, err) is run, which restores req->src and req->nbytes to the caller original values, stores the last (err + nonzero) bytes of the input as the new cache when err >= 0 (err is the number of bytes the update left unprocessed) and an empty cache and the same negative error when err < 0, restores the caller completion and data, and returns 0 or the negative error from the update op.

name: crypto_register_alg
prose: Precondition: alg is a fully set-up struct crypto_alg not yet registered; the caller may sleep (GFP_KERNEL allocation, down_write(&crypto_alg_sem)). The caller holds no reference of its own: the registration owns the single initial reference (cra_refcnt is set to 1 by crypto_check_alg). Postcondition: it first clears CRYPTO_ALG_DEAD in alg->cra_flags. Returns the negative errno from crypto_check_alg (-EINVAL for empty name or driver name, bad alignmask or blocksize, or negative priority) with nothing changed and no reference dropped. If CRYPTO_ALG_DUP_FIRST is set and cra_destroy is NULL it registers a kmemdup copy of the algorithm instead (cra_destroy = crypto_free_alg), returning -ENOMEM if that allocation fails (nothing registered, no reference dropped). Otherwise under crypto_alg_sem write lock it calls __crypto_register_alg, which fails with -EAGAIN if alg is dead, -EEXIST if alg is already listed or its names conflict with a non-moribund registered algorithm or larval, or the error of crypto_alloc_test_larval (-ENOMEM, or -ENOENT if a module reference on alg cannot be taken); on any of these failures the reference on alg is dropped with crypto_alg_put and the error is returned, nothing is registered. On success alg is on crypto_alg_list and 0 is returned: either no self-test is needed (CRYPTO_ALG_TESTED set and registration finished immediately, replacing lower-priority same-name algorithms) or a test larval is added and, if boot tests are finished, its test is scheduled with crypto_schedule_test, else the list of algorithms to put is released with crypto_remove_final.

name: _aead_recvmsg
prose: Precondition: sock->sk is an AF_ALG AEAD socket (with its parent socket holding the aead transform) and the caller holds lock_sock on it; the function may sleep. Postcondition: if no data has been initialised or more data is expected it first waits via af_alg_wait_for_data and returns any non-zero error from it (for example -EAGAIN). Then it returns -EINVAL if ctx->used < aead_assoclen + (tag size when decrypting); otherwise outlen = used + tag size (encrypt) or used - tag size (decrypt), where used includes the AAD. It allocates the async request (returning its error), copies the IV, obtains the output scatterlist with af_alg_get_rsgl (returning its error, after freeing resources) and if the caller output space (usedpages) is smaller than outlen reduces outlen and the input length used by the shortfall, returning -EINVAL if used would be left smaller than the shortfall plus (tag size when decrypting). It then allocates the TX scatterlist for processed = used + aead_assoclen bytes (-ENOMEM on failure), pulls exactly those processed bytes (AAD plus input) out of the socket TX list, copies the AAD to the output, and submits encrypt or decrypt. For an asynchronous kiocb it takes an extra sock reference; if the operation returns -EINPROGRESS the function returns -EIOCBQUEUED immediately and the request resources and the sock reference are released later by af_alg_async_cb; otherwise (completed or failed at once) the extra sock reference is dropped and processing continues to cleanup. For a synchronous request it waits with crypto_wait_req. On every path other than -EIOCBQUEUED af_alg_free_resources frees the request and its scatterlists, and the function returns the crypto error (for example -EBADMSG for a failed authentication tag) if non-zero, else outlen (the number of bytes written to the caller output).

name: aead_recvmsg
prose: Precondition: sock->sk is an AF_ALG AEAD socket and the caller does not hold its socket lock; the function sleeps. Postcondition: takes lock_sock(sk) and releases it with release_sock before returning on every path, and calls af_alg_wmem_wakeup(sk) before releasing. It loops while msg_data_left(msg) is non-zero, calling _aead_recvmsg and adding each positive result to the running total ret. When a call returns err <= 0 the loop ends: ret is set to err if err is -EIOCBQUEUED or -EBADMSG (discarding any bytes already accumulated) or if ret is still 0 (so a 0 result or an error at the first call is returned as is); otherwise ret keeps the number of bytes already produced. The function returns ret: 0 if msg_data_left(msg) was already 0 or the first _aead_recvmsg returned 0, otherwise the total number of bytes produced, or one of the errors above. After a -EIOCBQUEUED return an asynchronous request is in flight whose callback completes it and drops its sock reference.

name: _skcipher_recvmsg
prose: Precondition: sock->sk is an AF_ALG skcipher socket (its parent holds the skcipher transform), the caller holds lock_sock on it and the function may sleep. Postcondition: if the context is not initialised, or more data is expected while ctx->used is below the chunksize bs, it waits with af_alg_wait_for_data and returns any non-zero error. It allocates the request (returning PTR_ERR on failure), maps the caller output with af_alg_get_rsgl for up to ctx->used bytes (error returned after cleanup) giving len bytes; if more data is expected or len < ctx->used it returns -EINVAL when len < bs, otherwise rounds len down to a multiple of bs and marks the request CRYPTO_SKCIPHER_REQ_NOTFINAL. It allocates the TX scatterlist (-ENOMEM on failure), pulls len bytes from the socket TX list, and, if a saved ctx->state exists, imports it into the request (always freeing and NULLing ctx->state; an import error is returned, otherwise the request is flagged CRYPTO_SKCIPHER_REQ_CONT). It then encrypts or decrypts and always waits synchronously with crypto_wait_req (so it never returns -EIOCBQUEUED); if that succeeds, algif_skcipher_export saves the cipher state in a newly allocated ctx->state when the request is not final (returning -ENOMEM if that allocation fails or the export error, with ctx->state freed and NULL). On every path past the allocation af_alg_free_resources frees the request. It returns the first non-zero error encountered, else len, the number of bytes processed and written to the output buffers (which are the bytes removed from the TX list); len may be 0.

name: cprng_reset
prose: Precondition: tfm is a valid crypto_rng transform of the ansi_cprng algorithm; seed is a pointer (only pointer arithmetic seed + DEFAULT_BLK_SZ is done before the length check, so no read happens for a too short slen) and, when slen >= DEFAULT_PRNG_KSZ + DEFAULT_BLK_SZ (32), seed is readable for slen bytes. Postcondition: if slen < 32 returns -EINVAL without touching the context. Otherwise calls reset_prng_context(prng, key = seed + 16, klen = 16, V = seed, DT = seed + 32 if slen >= 48 else NULL) which, under the context spinlock (bh disabled), sets the NEED_RESET flag, loads V and DT (DT zeroed when NULL), clears the random buffers and sets the cipher key; it returns -EINVAL if PRNG_NEED_RESET is still set afterwards (the setkey failed), else 0 with the context reseeded and PRNG_NEED_RESET cleared. No reference is acquired or released.

name: prng_mod_init
prose: Precondition: module init context; the algorithms in rng_algs are not yet registered. Postcondition: returns crypto_register_rngs(rng_algs, ARRAY_SIZE(rng_algs)): 0 if every algorithm in rng_algs was registered with crypto_register_rng, otherwise the negative errno of the first registration that failed, in which case all algorithms registered earlier in the array have been unregistered again so none remains registered. No lock or reference is held by the caller afterwards.

name: crypto_larval_wait
prose: Precondition: alg is the struct crypto_alg embedded in a struct crypto_larval and the caller owns one reference on it (which this function always consumes); type and mask are the lookup parameters; the caller may sleep (up to 60 seconds). Postcondition: if boot self-tests are not finished it starts the test for the larval, then waits killably for larval->completion with a 60 second timeout and examines larval->adult: if the wait is interrupted it yields ERR_PTR(-EINTR); on timeout it kills the larval if it is a test larval and yields ERR_PTR(-ETIMEDOUT); if the adult is NULL or ERR_PTR(-EEXIST) it re-looks the algorithm up by name and yields the found algorithm (with a reference) or else ERR_PTR(-EEXIST) when the adult was -EEXIST, ERR_PTR(-EAGAIN) when it was NULL; any other ERR_PTR stored in larval->adult is passed through unchanged; if the larval is a test larval and the adult lacks CRYPTO_ALG_TESTED, or the adult has CRYPTO_ALG_FIPS_INTERNAL, or crypto_mod_get(adult) fails, it yields ERR_PTR(-EAGAIN); otherwise it yields the adult with a new module and algorithm reference taken by crypto_mod_get. In every case the caller reference on the larval is dropped with crypto_mod_put before returning. If the result is not an error but is itself a larval, the whole procedure repeats on it. The returned pointer is therefore a non-larval algorithm holding a reference owned by the caller, or an ERR_PTR with no reference held.

name: pkcs7_verify
prose: Precondition: pkcs7 is a parsed PKCS#7 message (its signed_infos list may be empty) and usage is any enum key_being_used_for value; the caller keeps ownership of pkcs7. Postcondition: usage is checked first: for VERIFYING_MODULE_SIGNATURE it returns -EKEYREJECTED unless data_type is OID_data and there are no authenticated attributes; for VERIFYING_FIRMWARE_SIGNATURE -EKEYREJECTED unless data_type is OID_data and authenticated attributes are present; for VERIFYING_KEXEC_PE_SIGNATURE -EKEYREJECTED unless data_type is OID_msIndirectData; for VERIFYING_UNSPECIFIED_SIGNATURE and VERIFYING_BPF_SIGNATURE -EKEYREJECTED unless data_type is OID_data; any other usage returns -EINVAL. Then every signed info is verified in list order with pkcs7_verify_one. A signed info marked blacklisted never causes an error return: if no other result has been recorded yet the result becomes -EKEYREJECTED and the loop continues (whatever pkcs7_verify_one returned for it is ignored). For a non-blacklisted signed info, a result of -ENOPKG marks sinfo->unsupported_crypto and continues, any other negative result is returned immediately (even if earlier signed infos verified), and a result of 0 sets the overall result to 0 (overriding any earlier -EKEYREJECTED) and continues. On completion the function returns 0 if at least one non-blacklisted signed info verified, otherwise -EKEYREJECTED if some signed info was blacklisted, otherwise -ENOPKG (including the empty-list case).

name: async_tx_channel_switch
prose: Precondition: depend_tx and tx are valid dma_async_tx_descriptors, depend_tx has a valid channel, tx has not yet been submitted and is to run after depend_tx completes; the caller keeps ownership of both descriptors. Postcondition: returns nothing. Under the depend_tx lock, if depend_tx still has a parent and depend_tx->chan == tx->chan, tx is chained after depend_tx and the function then calls device_issue_pending on the channel and returns. Otherwise, if the device has DMA_INTERRUPT capability it prepares an interrupt descriptor (no callback); if that preparation succeeds, tx is chained to it and then, under the depend_tx lock, if depend_tx still has a parent the interrupt descriptor is chained after depend_tx and acked, else (no parent) its parent is cleared and it is submitted and acked; in both cases device_issue_pending is then called on depend_tx channel. If the device lacks DMA_INTERRUPT or the preparation returns NULL, the function waits synchronously for depend_tx with dma_wait_for_async_tx, panics (never returns) if the wait result is not DMA_COMPLETE, and otherwise submits tx directly with tx_submit.

name: raid6_test
prose: Precondition: runs once as a module init function; may sleep. Postcondition: allocates NDISKS + 3 = 67 pages (NDISKS is 64) into data[] with GFP_KERNEL; if an allocation fails it releases the pages already allocated and returns -ENOMEM. Otherwise it runs the recovery tests for 4, 5, 11, 12, 24 and 64 disks (those whose count does not exceed NDISKS are run; individual test failures are only counted and logged), prints a summary, releases all 67 pages and returns 0. It returns 0 even if tests failed, and no page, lock or other resource remains held afterwards.

name: crypto_authenc_esn_setauthsize
prose: Precondition: none; authsize is any unsigned int (the authenc_esn transform argument is not used). Postcondition: returns -EINVAL (-22) when authsize is between 1 and 3 inclusive, and 0 when authsize is 0 or at least 4. No state is read or changed and no lock, reference or memory is acquired or released.

name: chachapoly_setauthsize
prose: Precondition: none; authsize is any unsigned int (the tfm argument is not used). Postcondition: returns 0 if authsize equals POLY1305_DIGEST_SIZE (16) and -EINVAL (-22) for every other value. No state is read or changed and no lock, reference or memory is acquired or released.

name: chachapoly_create
prose: Precondition: tmpl and tb are the template and its attributes, name is the template name ("rfc7539" or "rfc7539esp" style) and ivsize the IV size; the caller may sleep. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL immediately if ivsize > CHACHAPOLY_IV_SIZE (12), without allocating. Then returns the error of crypto_check_attr_type(tb, CRYPTO_ALG_TYPE_AEAD, &mask) if it is non-zero (no allocation yet). Otherwise it allocates an aead instance (-ENOMEM on failure), grabs the chacha skcipher named in tb[1] (error returned), reads the poly name from tb[2] (its error returned) and fails with -EINVAL if that name is not "poly1305" or "poly1305-generic", if the chacha IV size is not CHACHA_IV_SIZE (16) or its blocksize is not 1, or with -ENAMETOOLONG if either composed algorithm name is too long. Otherwise it fills in the instance (names, priority, alignmask, context size including the salt, ivsize, chunksize, maxauthsize = POLY1305_DIGEST_SIZE, the ops and chachapoly_setauthsize) and calls aead_register_instance; on success it returns 0 and the instance is owned by the crypto subsystem; if registration fails, or on any failure after the allocation, the instance (including the grabbed skcipher spawn) is released with chachapoly_free and the negative errno is returned.

name: crypto_pump_requests
prose: Precondition: engine is an initialised crypto_engine (kworker, pump_requests work, queue and queue_lock set up); the caller does not hold engine->queue_lock; in_kthread says whether the caller is the pump kthread worker. Postcondition: returns nothing; engine->queue_lock is taken with interrupts saved and is not held on any return. If engine->retry_support is false and engine->cur_req is already set, nothing is changed. Else if the queue is empty or engine->running is false: if engine->busy is false nothing is done; otherwise if !in_kthread the pump work is queued on the kworker (to be run later) and nothing else changes, and if in_kthread engine->busy is cleared. Otherwise it takes the backlog entry (crypto_get_backlog) and dequeues a request; if the dequeue returns NULL it returns. Without retry_support the dequeued request becomes engine->cur_req. It sets engine->busy, drops the lock and calls the algorithm do_one_request op on the request. If that returns a negative value: for retry_support with -ENOSPC the request is put back at the head of the queue under the lock, the pump work is queued, and the function returns without completing the backlog request; for any other negative value (or without retry_support) an error is logged and the request is completed with that error via crypto_request_complete. On a non-negative return the request is left for the driver to complete. In every path that did not requeue, a backlog request, if one was taken, is completed with -EINPROGRESS, and then, if retry_support is set, the lock is retaken and the function loops back to dequeue the next request; otherwise it returns.

name: crypto_cts_create
prose: Precondition: tmpl is the cts template and tb the template attribute array, with the wrapped algorithm name in tb[1]; the caller may sleep. Postcondition: returns the error of crypto_check_attr_type(tb, CRYPTO_ALG_TYPE_SKCIPHER, &mask) if non-zero, before allocating anything; returns -ENOMEM if the instance allocation fails. Otherwise it grabs the underlying skcipher named in tb[1] (its error returned), and returns -EINVAL if that algorithm IV size differs from its block size or its name does not start with "cbc(". It sets the instance name with crypto_inst_setname (its error, for example -ENAMETOOLONG, returned), copies priority, blocksize, alignmask, chunksize and key sizes, sets ivsize to the block size and installs the cts ops. It then calls skcipher_register_instance: on success it returns 0 and the instance is owned by the crypto subsystem; if registration fails, or any step after the allocation failed, the instance and its spawn are released with crypto_cts_free and the negative errno is returned. Mismatching algorithms are not a precondition: they yield -EINVAL.

name: drbg_ctr_update
prose: Precondition: drbg is an initialised CTR DRBG state (ctr_handle is a keyed-capable skcipher; drbg->C, drbg->V and drbg->scratchpad are allocated with the scratchpad large enough for the temp area of statelen + blocklen bytes followed by df_data of statelen bytes); seed is NULL or a valid list of seed buffers; reseed is the update mode (0, 1, 2, or 3 and above). Postcondition: if reseed < 3, df_data is zeroed first. If reseed == 0, drbg->V is incremented as a counter and the skcipher key is set from drbg->C (drbg->C itself is only read, never modified), and a setkey error is returned. If seed is non-NULL, df_data is filled by drbg_ctr_df from the seed (its error returned). Then the keystream temp = CTR encryption of df_data is produced with drbg_kcapi_sym_ctr; if that fails its error is returned immediately and the scratchpad is NOT wiped. Otherwise the skcipher key is set to the first keylen bytes of temp (setkey error returned), drbg->V is set to the next blocklen bytes of temp and incremented by one, and 0 is returned. On every exit other than the drbg_kcapi_sym_ctr failure the temp area (statelen + blocklen bytes) is zeroed and df_data is zeroed unless reseed == 2. No lock or reference is acquired or released.

name: ecdh_init
prose: Precondition: module initialisation context. Postcondition: it registers the KPP algorithms ecdh_nist_p192, ecdh_nist_p256 and ecdh_nist_p384 in that order. The result of registering p192 is only recorded in ecdh_nist_p192_registered and does not affect the return value. If p256 registration fails it returns that negative errno (and unregisters p192 if p192 had been registered); if p384 registration fails it unregisters p256, then p192 if it had been registered, and returns the p384 negative errno. If both p256 and p384 register it returns 0, even when p192 failed to register. On a non-zero return no algorithm of this module remains registered.

name: krb5_selftest
prose: Real function is krb5_selftest(void) (the enclosing function, not shown in the excerpt). Precondition: none beyond process context (it may sleep). Postcondition: allocates a 4096-byte scratch buffer with kmalloc(GFP_KERNEL) and returns -ENOMEM if that fails. Otherwise it runs, in order, every PRF test, key test, encryption test and MIC test in the tables (re-filling the scratch buffer with 0x5a before each encryption and MIC test); a test returning -EOPNOTSUPP is skipped with a notice, and the first other negative result stops the run and is returned. If no test failed it returns 0. A "succeeded" or "failed" message is logged and the scratch buffer is freed on every path after its allocation.
note: Slice cuts the function head; real name krb5_selftest is not in the slice. Previous prose omitted the PRF tests.

name: pkcs1pad_create
prose: Precondition: tmpl is the pkcs1pad template and tb is its attribute array with the name of the wrapped akcipher algorithm in tb[1]; the caller may sleep. Postcondition: returns the error of crypto_check_attr_type(tb, CRYPTO_ALG_TYPE_AKCIPHER, &mask) if non-zero, or -ENOMEM if the instance allocation fails, in both cases before any instance exists so nothing is freed. Otherwise it grabs the named akcipher (error returned), returns -EINVAL if that algorithm cra_name is not exactly "rsa", and -ENAMETOOLONG if either "pkcs1pad(<cra_name>)" or "pkcs1pad(<cra_driver_name>)" does not fit in CRYPTO_MAX_ALG_NAME. Otherwise it copies the priority, sets the context size and installs the pkcs1pad ops (init, exit, encrypt, decrypt, set_pub_key, set_priv_key, max_size) and calls akcipher_register_instance: on success it returns 0 and the instance is owned by the crypto subsystem; if registration fails, or any step after the allocation failed, the instance and its spawn are released with pkcs1pad_free and the negative errno is returned.

name: skcipher_walk_done
prose: Precondition: walk is a valid skcipher_walk whose current step was set up by skcipher_walk_first or skcipher_walk_next (walk->nbytes bytes mapped, or 0 if the walk is finished), and res is a negative errno or the number of bytes of the step left unprocessed (0 <= res <= walk->nbytes). Postcondition: let n = walk->nbytes. If n == 0 the walk is just cleaned up (see below) with walk->total unchanged and res returned unchanged. Otherwise, if res >= 0 the processed count is n - res and the new total is walk->total - (n - res); if res < 0 the count used is the full n and the new total is 0. According to the flags: with no SLOW, COPY or DIFF flag the source walk is advanced by the count and the destination walk is finished by the count; with DIFF the source is finished and the destination finished; with COPY the source is advanced, the destination is mapped, the count bytes are copied from walk->page into it, and it is finished; in the SLOW case the source walk is not touched here: if res > 0 the result becomes -EINVAL and the new total 0 (nothing is copied), else the count bytes are copied from the walk buffer to the destination with memcpy_to_scatterwalk. Then a positive res is turned into 0, walk->total is set to the new total and walk->nbytes to 0. If the new total is non-zero it (with cond_resched when SKCIPHER_WALK_SLEEP is set) clears the SLOW, COPY and DIFF flags and returns skcipher_walk_next(walk) (0, -EINVAL or -ENOMEM). If the new total is 0 the walk is cleaned up and the (non-positive) res is returned. Cleanup: if walk->buffer or walk->page is non-NULL, the IV is copied back to walk->oiv if walk->iv differs from it, walk->buffer is kfree'd unless it equals walk->page, and walk->page is freed; if both are NULL nothing is freed.

name: crypto_hmac_sha256_export
prose: Precondition: desc is a valid shash_desc whose HMAC-SHA256 context is initialised and out points to a writable buffer of at least the algorithm statesize. Postcondition: exports only the inner SHA-256 state HMAC_SHA256_CTX(desc)->ctx.sha_ctx through __crypto_sha256_export (the bytecount rounded down to a block boundary and the count of buffered partial bytes are stored; the outer key state ostate is not exported) and returns that function result, which is always 0. The context is not modified and no lock or reference is acquired or released.

name: crypto_sha256_mod_init
prose: Precondition: module initialisation context; the algorithms in the static algs table are not yet registered. Postcondition: returns crypto_register_shashes(algs, ARRAY_SIZE(algs)): 0 if every shash algorithm in algs (sha224, sha256, hmac(sha224), hmac(sha256), library-backed) was registered, otherwise a negative errno, in which case the algorithms registered earlier in the table have been unregistered again. No lock or reference is held afterwards.

name: __crypto_shash_import
prose: Precondition: desc->tfm is a valid shash transform, in points to a readable exported state of that algorithm (at least ss bytes where ss = crypto_shash_statesize(tfm), reduced by blocksize + 1 for block-only algorithms), and import is the algorithm import callback or NULL. Postcondition: returns -ENOKEY without touching the descriptor if the transform has CRYPTO_TFM_NEED_KEY set. Otherwise, for a block-only transform, the last byte of the descriptor context (buf[descsize - 1], the buffered-byte count) is set to 0 in both of the following cases; then if import is NULL it copies ss bytes (the state size, minus blocksize + 1 for a block-only transform) from in into the descriptor context and returns 0, and if import is non-NULL it returns import(desc, in) unchanged. No lock or reference is acquired or released.

name: crypto_shash_import
prose: Precondition: desc->tfm is a valid shash transform and in points to a readable state exported from the same algorithm (crypto_shash_statesize(tfm) bytes). Postcondition: err = __crypto_shash_import(desc, in, alg->import), so -ENOKEY if the transform needs a key, else 0 or the import callback result. If the transform is block-only (this step runs even when err is non-zero), it additionally copies the last blocksize + 1 bytes of the exported state (in + statesize - plen) to the end of the descriptor context (buf + descsize - plen), and if the resulting buffered-byte count buf[descsize - 1] is >= blocksize + 1 it sets err = -EOVERFLOW; otherwise err is unchanged. Returns err. No lock or reference is acquired or released.

name: valid_sg_divisions
prose: Precondition: divs points to count readable struct test_sg_division entries (it may be any pointer when count is 0) and flags_ret points to a writable int. Postcondition: scans entries from index 0 while i < count and the running total of proportion_of_total differs from TEST_SG_TOTAL (10000). For each scanned entry whose proportion_of_total is <= 0 or exceeds TEST_SG_TOTAL minus the running total the function returns false immediately, without examining that entry flush_type or nosimd; otherwise the proportion is added to the total and *flags_ret gets SGDIVS_HAVE_FLUSHES ORed in if the entry flush_type != FLUSH_TYPE_NONE and SGDIVS_HAVE_NOSIMD ORed in if its nosimd is true (existing bits of *flags_ret are preserved; bits are only ever set, so entries scanned before a failing entry may already have contributed flags). When the scan stops it returns true if and only if the total equals TEST_SG_TOTAL and all bytes of the remaining entries divs[i .. count-1] are zero (memchr_inv finds no non-zero byte), and false otherwise. It writes nothing else and acquires or releases no lock or reference.

name: calibrate_xor_blocks
prose: Precondition: module initialisation context; may sleep; at least one XOR template is available on the measuring path. Postcondition: first asks the architecture with XOR_SELECT_TEMPLATE(NULL); if that returns a template, an informational message is logged, active_template is set to it and 0 is returned, with no memory allocated. Otherwise it allocates a 4-page (order 2) benchmark buffer with GFP_KERNEL; if that fails it logs a warning and returns -ENOMEM leaving active_template (and template_list) unchanged. Otherwise it resets template_list, benchmarks all candidate templates with do_xor_speed, selects the template with the highest speed (the first in list order among equals), logs it, frees the benchmark pages, sets active_template to the selected template and returns 0.

name: v9fs_iop_set_acl
prose: Precondition: dentry has a valid inode; acl is NULL (remove the ACL) or a valid posix_acl and type is ACL_TYPE_ACCESS or ACL_TYPE_DEFAULT; the caller keeps its own reference to acl (this function does not take or drop one); the function may sleep. Postcondition: the temporary xattr buffer is always freed. If acl is non-NULL it is validated with posix_acl_valid (its error returned) and converted to xattr form into a GFP_NOFS buffer (-ENOMEM if the allocation fails, or the posix_acl_to_xattr error). If the mount access mode is not V9FS_ACCESS_CLIENT it returns the result of v9fs_xattr_set(dentry, name, value, size, 0) without updating the cached ACL. In client access mode: -EOPNOTSUPP if the inode is a symlink; -EPERM if the caller is neither owner nor capable; for ACL_TYPE_ACCESS with a non-NULL acl it computes the new mode with posix_acl_update_mode (its error returned), turns the xattr value into NULL (removal) if the ACL is exactly representable by the mode bits, and applies the mode with v9fs_vfs_setattr_dotl whose result is ignored; for ACL_TYPE_DEFAULT on a non-directory it returns -EINVAL if acl is non-NULL and 0 if acl is NULL without setting anything. Finally it calls v9fs_xattr_set and, only if that returns 0, caches acl (the original argument, possibly NULL) in the inode with set_cached_acl; it returns the v9fs_xattr_set result.

name: v9fs_vfs_create_dotl
prose: Precondition: dir is a valid directory inode on a 9p mount, dentry is a negative dentry in it with a parent fid obtainable, omode gives the file type and permission bits, excl is not used; the caller holds the directory inode lock and the function may sleep. Postcondition: returns v9fs_vfs_mknod_dotl(idmap, dir, dentry, omode, 0), i.e. creates the node with device number 0 through the 9P Tmknod_dotl request: it returns 0 after the server created the node, the directory attribute cache was invalidated, a new inode was obtained, the default/access ACLs set up and the dentry instantiated with the new inode and its fid; otherwise it returns the negative errno from the parent-fid lookup, ACL mode computation, the mknod request, the walk or the inode creation, leaving the dentry uninstantiated. The temporary fids and ACL references taken are released on every path.
note: Slice cuts the function head; previous prose described a different function (atomic_open).

name: adfs_fplus_iterate
prose: Precondition: dir is a loaded big directory (dir->bighead valid) and ctx is a valid dir_context; the caller holds whatever lock protects the directory. Postcondition: always returns 0. If (ctx->pos - 2) >> 32 is non-zero (ctx->pos < 2, since the signed difference is negative, or ctx->pos - 2 >= 2^32) it returns at once emitting nothing. Otherwise it calls adfs_fplus_setpos(dir, ctx->pos - 2), which fails (and the function returns emitting nothing) when ctx->pos - 2 is greater than the big directory entry count, else sets dir->pos = ctx->pos - 2. It then repeatedly reads the entry at dir->pos with adfs_fplus_getnext (which advances dir->pos on success); for each entry read it calls dir_emit(ctx, name, name_len, indaddr, DT_UNKNOWN); if dir_emit returns false it stops (that entry is consumed from dir->pos but ctx->pos is not advanced for it), otherwise ctx->pos is incremented by one. It also stops when getnext fails (end of directory or a read error). No lock or reference is acquired or released.

name: lookup_zone
prose: Precondition: dm is a valid disc map zone whose buffer head data (dm->dm_bh->b_data) is loaded and whose start and end bits (dm_startbit, dm_endbit) delimit a well-formed fragment list; idlen is the fragment id length in bits (1 <= idlen < 32); frag_id is the id to look for; offset points to a writable unsigned int giving the bit offset to find among the fragments with that id. Postcondition: the fragments of the zone are scanned in order from dm_startbit; the free-space link chain fragments (those at the positions given by the free link) are skipped and never matched; for each other fragment whose id equals frag_id and which has length L = fragment end bit + 1 - start bit, if *offset < L the function returns start + *offset (the bit number holding that offset) and *offset is left at its current value, which is the original value minus the lengths of all matching fragments skipped before it; otherwise *offset is decreased by L and the scan continues. It returns -1 if the scan reaches the end of the zone without finding such a fragment (the original *offset was at least the total length of all matching fragments; *offset is then the original minus that total), or if a fragment extends to or past dm_endbit, in which case an "oversized fragment" error is also logged and *offset is left reduced by the matches skipped so far. No lock or reference is acquired or released.

name: affs_init_bitmap
prose: Real function is affs_init_bitmap(sb, flags). Precondition: sb is an AFFS super_block whose sbi->s_root_bh buffer head is held and valid, sbi->s_partition_size and s_reserved are set so that the bitmap count is at least 1, and flags points to the writable mount flags; the function may sleep. Postcondition: if *flags has SB_RDONLY it returns 0 immediately and changes nothing. If the root block bm_flag is 0 it logs a notice, sets SB_RDONLY in *flags and returns 0. Otherwise it initialises s_last_bmap, s_bmap_bh, s_bmap_bits and s_bmap_count and allocates sbi->s_bitmap with kzalloc (GFP_KERNEL), returning -ENOMEM with s_bitmap NULL on failure. It then reads each bitmap block (following the root block pointers and the bitmap extension blocks), recording its key and free-bit count (memweight): a block that cannot be read gives -EIO, an extension block that cannot be read gives -EIO, and a bitmap block with a bad checksum logs a warning, sets SB_RDONLY in *flags and returns 0, in all three cases leaving s_bitmap allocated and only partly filled (it is not freed here). On full success it masks the unused bits of the last bitmap block, zeroes its remaining words, rewrites its checksum, marks it dirty, recomputes that block free-bit count and returns 0. All buffer heads read by this function (the current bitmap block and any extension block) are released before return on every path after allocation; whenever s_bitmap is non-NULL on return the caller is responsible for freeing it with affs_free_bitmap.
note: Slice cuts the function head, so the name affs_init_bitmap is not in the slice.

name: affs_readdir
prose: Precondition: file is an open AFFS directory whose private_data points to a valid struct affs_dir_data (allocated by affs_dir_open); ctx->pos is 0 or 1 for the start, or encodes the resume position as ((hash_pos << 16) | chain_pos) + 2; the caller holds the usual directory read serialisation (inode lock shared); may sleep. Postcondition: if ctx->pos < 2 it resets data->ino to 0 and emits "." and ".." with dir_emit_dots, returning 0 immediately (before taking the directory lock) if the emit fails. It then takes the AFFS directory lock, released before return on every path after that. A chain_pos of 0xffff logs a warning and moves to the start of the next hash bucket. If the directory header block cannot be read it returns 0 without emitting. If data->ino is set and the directory inode version equals data->cookie it resumes directly at block data->ino; otherwise it walks hash_pos chain chain_pos entries (a failed block read here is logged and makes the function return -EIO) and, if the chain is shorter, continues with the following hash buckets. Entries are emitted with dir_emit(name, namelen, block number, DT_UNKNOWN) and ctx->pos incremented per emitted entry, ctx->pos being set to the start of each new bucket; if dir_emit returns false the loop ends. A failed read of an entry block while emitting is logged and only ends the current chain (emission continues with the next non-empty hash bucket). On the way out data->cookie is set to the current inode version and data->ino to the block number of the entry where emission stopped (0 when everything was emitted). All buffer heads are released. The return value is 0, or -EIO only for the failed block read while skipping to the resume position in the chain.

name: affs_write_end_ofs
prose: Real function: write_end for the OFS (old file system) address space; it copies the first len bytes of the page data at in-page offset pos & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) into the file chain of OFS data blocks (copied is ignored). Precondition: folio is locked, uptodate and holds the data of the write, referenced by the caller; mapping->host is an OFS inode; the caller does not use folio afterwards because this function unlocks it and drops the reference. Postcondition: the data is written block by block: a leading partial block (when the position is not block aligned) is read with affs_bread_ino and updated in place (its size field raised to cover the data, checksum fixed, buffer dirtied); then each whole block is obtained with affs_getemptyblk_ino and filled; then a trailing partial block is read or created with affs_bread_ino; for newly created blocks the data header is initialised (type, key, sequence, size, next) and linked from the previous block next pointer. If the first block cannot be read it returns that negative errno with nothing written (and the folio unlocked and put). Otherwise it marks the folio uptodate (unless an error occurred), releases the block buffer, extends inode->i_size and mmu_private to the end of the written data if larger, clears the FIBF_ARCHIVED protection bit (marking the inode dirty) if set, unlocks and puts the folio, and returns the number of bytes written. If allocating or reading a later block fails after some bytes were written it returns the bytes written so far; if nothing was written yet it returns PTR_ERR of the previous block buffer pointer (0 when there is none), a latent quirk of the code. No lock besides the folio lock is taken.
note: Previously dropped as non-function; it is a real function. Slice has the function.

name: afs_manage_cell
prose: Precondition: cell is a valid afs_cell that the caller (the cell manager work item) holds a reference on, with cell->net valid; may sleep. Postcondition: returns true if and only if the cell was removed on this call, in which case under net->cells_lock it was set to AFS_CELL_REMOVING, deactivated, its servers purged and itself erased from net->cells, then its root volume reference was dropped (cell->root_volume = NULL) and the state set to AFS_CELL_DEAD, so the caller must drop the cell final reference; removal happens when the cell is in AFS_CELL_SETTING_UP and afs_activate_cell fails (cell->error is set to the negative errno), or when the cell is active-capable (UNLOOKED or ACTIVE, or newly set up) and afs_has_cell_expired reports it expired (it has no active users and either the network is no longer live or its garbage collection delay has passed), unless cell->active becomes non-zero before the cells_lock is taken, in which case removal is abandoned and the active-cell handling is done instead. Otherwise it returns false: for AFS_CELL_REMOVING (with WARN_ON_ONCE), AFS_CELL_DEAD, or an unknown state (with WARN_ON_ONCE) nothing is changed; for a live cell, a successful activation moves SETTING_UP to UNLOOKED, a pending AFS_CELL_FL_DO_LOOKUP flag is cleared and afs_update_cell run (a failure stores the negative errno in cell->error), an UNLOOKED cell becomes ACTIVE after that lookup step, and if the cell has an expiry time and the network is live the cell is requeued immediately (if the time has passed) or the cell timer is set for the remaining time.
